note: Archive adversarial acceptance coverage-completeness manifest (cinatra#1943). Every row is one literal criterion from #1943's issue body (15 total, verbatim from the issue — see the gate script's CANONICAL_CRITERIA). This is NOT a scanned-surface manifest (contrast scripts/audit/system-writer-manifest.json): rows are hand-authored against the issue text, not discovered by a source scan, so there is no --write-manifest regeneration mode. `owner: "sibling"` rows point at a SIBLING slice's own test (w3-1939 / r-1940) via ciDependency rather than re-authoring it — #1943 never duplicates a criterion another slice's acceptance map already proves. `status` is a DECLARED claim: it may read "green" only once the gate's `strict` mode structurally confirms the referenced proof(s) exist, AND the coverage-gate's own CI job `needs:` the job named in ciDependency. Every row ALSO carries a `negativeControl` once green — the RED half of the issue's "each its own RED-THEN-GREEN test": the counterpart run in which the OUTCOME INVERTS once the one guard under test is removed. For a row whose proof is a refusal claim that means the same payload LANDS unguarded; for a row whose proof is a success claim (lease settle, eventual archive under contention) it means the same operation is REFUSED in the state that lacks the precondition. Either way a green row can never rest on a claim nothing could have falsified (see the gate script's CONTROL_KIND comment for why this is enforced mechanically rather than recorded in PR prose). Regenerate NOTHING — edit this file by hand, one row per criterion.

kernelProof.testName: a cast cannot forge a VerifiedRunRef

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 1): a shape-only verifier ACCEPTS the very ref isVerifiedRunRef rejects — the brand, not the shape, is what refuses

kernelProof.testName: a forged execution-attempt id (well-typed but not the leased one) is refused

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 2): the SAME forged attempt id lands the write when the SAME body runs outside guardedRunWrite — the seam, not the payload, is what refuses

kernelProof.testName: ticket replay across an unarchive/re-archive cycle: a stale ticket never un-refuses, and a fresh ticket at the new epoch redeems (positive control)

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 3): with the archive-epoch clause removed, the SAME stale ticket passes every other kernel check and would redeem — the epoch, not staleness of any other kind, is what refuses

kernelProof.testName: delete-vs-completion race: a run.complete write queued behind a guarded delete's exclusive fence sees the committed delete, never landing into a deleted org

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 4): the SAME sentinel completion write, issued UNGUARDED, is never queued behind the delete's fence — it commits mid-delete and its row outlives the deleted org

kernelProof.testName: platform-admin denial: an unconditionally-permissive authority is still refused for a mismatched org (org-scope beats any elevated capability bit)

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 5): the SAME permissive authority, differing ONLY in the org it is scoped to, lands the SAME write through the SAME kernel guard

kernelProof.testName: a real job's authority stripped post-hoc via Object.assign is refused at dispatch and never runs its handler

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 6): the identically-stripped handler RUNS when invoked directly, bypassing dispatchRegisteredJob's authority check

kernelProof.testName: two-connection post-check race: a guarded write blocks behind the lifecycle locks, then LOSES to the committed archive (capability-denied)

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 7): the SAME sentinel write, issued UNGUARDED, neither blocks on the lifecycle locks nor re-reads the state — it lands into the org that is mid-archive

kernelProof.testName: every real mintable job refuses every purpose NOT in its own declared allowedPurposes

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 8): the SAME foreign job, purpose, org and payload MINTS real capabilities once its allowedPurposes AND capabilities declarations are both tampered — each check refuses on its own, neither is redundant

rows.criterion: Pre-archive parent spawning post-archive child denied

kernelProof.testName: a child-run creation blocked behind an in-progress archive LOSES the race: refused, and no child row ever lands

negativeControl.testName: positive control: a child run created BEFORE any archive succeeds normally (the guard isn't vacuously refusing everything)

kernelProof.testName: a2aTaskId present, cancel CONFIRMED ⇒ settles this tick, in DB-call order

negativeControl.testName: a2aTaskId present, cancel THROWS, attempts below threshold ⇒ deferred, NO settle this tick

e2eProof.testName: a genuinely expired lease on a non-terminal run settles to a typed FAILURE, never a bare denial — real CAS + real lease DELETE

kernelProof.testName: archived org + held lease + run.complete ⇒ CAS + meta + lease DELETE commit together

negativeControl.testName: archived org + terminal edge but NO held lease ⇒ refused, no CAS, no settle

kernelProof.testName: interleaving 1 — a queued member INSERT holds the org row's FOR SHARE lock first (org still active): the archive UPDATE genuinely BLOCKS behind it, and only lands after the insert commits

interleaving 2 — an in-flight (uncommitted) archive UPDATE holds the org row lock first: a concurrent member INSERT's FOR SHARE...NOWAIT fails IMMEDIATELY (55P03), never landing a row into what becomes an archived org

negativeControl.testName: negative control (row 12): with NO concurrent holder, the SAME member INSERT and the SAME archive UPDATE both succeed promptly — the blocking and the 55P03 come from the contention, not from either statement being unable to run

kernelProof.testName: ONE shared archive flip refuses ALL THREE surfaces for the identical org — in-process BA, raw-HTTP BA, and the app-native guard

negativeControl.testName: positive control: an ACTIVE org allows all three surfaces — neither transport is hard-coded to always-refuse

rows.criterion: BOUNDED, deterministic eventual-successful-archive under contention (a fixed retry ceiling, not an unbounded spin)

kernelProof.testName: bounded contention: a fixed, finite set of concurrent guarded writers never blocks the exclusive fence past a generous deadline, and the fence succeeds once the writers drain

e2eProof.testName: bounded contention against the REAL archiveOrganization action: a fixed, finite set of concurrent guarded writers never blocks it past a generous deadline, and it succeeds once they drain (Decision 8's two-phase criterion, e2e half)

negativeControl.testName: forced lock-exhaustion: every bounded attempt hits 55P03 under a continuously held fence → a typed busy error, never a hang and never a silent {ok:true} — then the SAME org archives successfully the instant contention clears (eventual success, the criterion's other half)

rows.criterion: 3-role live Playwright proof (owner archives/unarchives; admin/member read-only; non-member 404) on a production-equivalent build

e2eProof.testName: the owner archives the organization from the Danger zone and it goes read-only
the owner unarchives the organization and it is restored
an org admin is read-only on the archived organization and gets no archive control
an ordinary member sees the organization as archived, with no management or archive control
the same archive submission is refused by the action when it carries an org admin's or a member's session
a non-member gets a 404 on the archived organization's settings surface

negativeControl.testName: negative control: with the activation gate off, the same owner's same archive submission renders nothing and lands nothing
negative control: on the active organization the same admin and member see the state invert
negative control: the same admin session lands the same submission once its membership row says owner
negative control: the same non-member reaches the same organization once their membership row exists

rows.note: PROOF LANDED, ROW NOT YET CLAIMABLE — and the distinction is mechanical, not editorial. The spec and its four red halves above exist, are grep-verified by audit mode, and RUN: they live in tests/e2e/rbac/, which tests/e2e/config/rbac.config.ts globs, so build-image.yml's e2e-rbac job executes them with no workflow change. What is still missing is ONE structural edge: this gate's own job, archive-acceptance-gate, does not `needs: e2e-rbac`. strictCheckRow therefore reports a green claim on this row as unverifiable, and scripts/audit/__tests__/archive-acceptance-gate.test.mjs — which runs in the blocking `test` job — asserts that EVERY green row passes strictCheckRow with zero reasons. Flipping this row green before that edge exists would turn a blocking CI job red: a false claim the gate itself catches. Adding the edge is a .github/workflows change — a high-risk, maintainer-gated path this program deliberately keeps in its own sibling PR (PR #2703's Decision 6, where it is item 1 of three). The flip is then this one word, on the strength of a green e2e-rbac run: no test, no proof and no further CI work remains.
